name: Licensing regime for fiat-collateralised stablecoins
milestone: Regime set out in Payments System Vision 2028, 2026-06-17
position_end: A drafted issuer-licensing regime with reserve localisation; no instrument issued
note: the CBN frames stablecoins as on-chain representations of sovereign currency requiring monetary oversight distinct from e-money or crypto-assets, and models the regime on Hong Kong, MiCA, Japan and the United States: an issuer licence, 100% of naira-stablecoin reserves in cash, Treasury bills or equivalents with licensed Nigerian commercial banks, daily reconciliation and monthly audited reserve publication, and for foreign-currency stablecoins a minimum share of reserves held domestically with the balance in approved foreign custodians; the document also evaluates smart contracts for real-time regulatory visibility; no draft instrument or consultation is on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Payment Stack
position_end: ISO 20022 stack live with instant settlement
note: next-generation infrastructure on ISO 20022; the first live transaction ran on 2025-11-07 with instant settlement

subject: dpi.pay
name: NIBSS Instant Payments
position_end: 4.12bn transactions; rated the first African instant system of its class
note: electronic payments reached US$256bn by 2025-07 from US$187bn in 2024-08 across 4.12bn transactions, and SIIPS 2025 rated NIP the first African instant system to achieve mature inclusivity

subject: dpi.pay
name: Non-bank acquirer access to a global card network
position_end: A Nigerian payments company gained direct access to a global card network as a non-bank acquirer, letting it onboard licensed merchants for card acceptance across online, in-store and mobile channels without a bank sponsor
note: no merchant count, pricing or settlement arrangement is stated, and no central bank statement on non-bank acquiring is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Open banking
position_end: First in Africa; consented data sharing across about 120m bank customers
note: first in Africa, mandating consented customer-data sharing across about 120m bank customers through BVN-tied consent, a central registry and standardised APIs, four years after the framework

subject: dpi.pay
name: Securities regulator accelerated regulatory incubation programme
milestone: Three further firms named as admitted, reported 2026-08-17
position_end: Three further virtual-asset firms named as admitted in the week to 2026-08-17 - a payment solutions firm, an access provider and a card issuer - letting them test digital-asset services under supervision, on top of the twelve admitted since July. No graduation route, licensing outcome or supervisory condition is published
note: the counts across accounts overlap and are not reconciled: one of the three named on 2026-08-17 is the firm already recorded as admitted on 2026-08-14

subject: dpi.pay
name: Stablecoin business-to-business settlement rails
position_end: 1,500+ businesses across Nigeria and Kenya on dollar liquidity
note: a licensed local exchange plugged into Tether's dollar liquidity for cross-border settlement, reporting 1,500+ businesses across Nigeria and Kenya; the yield partners, rates and source are undisclosed, and dollarised settlement rails are marketed as an escape from dollar-denominated correspondent banking

subject: dpi.pay
name: USSD end-user billing
position_end: Billed to airtime at ₦6.98 per 120 seconds with opt-in
note: ended the multi-year telco-bank USSD debt dispute; session costs are billed to airtime at ₦6.98 per 120 seconds with real-time confirmation and opt-in

subject: dpi.pay
name: Withholding tax on creator-economy platform payouts
milestone: State revenue service pressing platforms to deduct at source, reported 2026-08-14
position_end: The Lagos State Internal Revenue Service is testing whether creator-economy platform payouts are royalties subject to 5% withholding tax and pressing two named platforms to deduct at source under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025; it follows the same authority’s earlier attempt to make a ride-hailing platform a value-added-tax collection agent. No assessment, ruling or judgment is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electronic civil registration and vital statistics
position_end: Nationwide; birth registration about 57% and death under 20%
sources: 2026-07-22-npc-nationwide-digital-birth-death-registration|2026-07-23-akwa-ibom-digital-civil-registration-system|2026-02-20 UNICEF records 14 million Nigeria birth registrations in two years
note: nationwide from 2026-07-01 on the VitalReg platform; birth registration about 57% and death under 20% as at 2026-07 against about 5m births a year, through 4,011 centres toward a target of about 8,000; newborn registration requires at least one parent to hold a valid NIN, and the register runs as a public-private partnership with a private contractor carrying availability and security duties

subject: dpi.registry
name: National alphanumeric digital postcode system
milestone: Launch date set at 2026-10-01, announced to the President 2026-08-04
position_end: A launch date of 2026-10-01 for a unique address per building, with integration to existing government identity databases to follow
note: explicitly property-level rather than cluster-level as in the UK, and the minister said integration with existing government identity databases would follow — no lawful basis, custodian or data-protection arrangement for that integration is stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Electronic Assets Register
position_end: Live

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Land Registration and Documentation Programme
position_end: More than 90% of land unregistered
note: more than 90% of land is unregistered, locking an estimated US$300bn as dead capital on the housing minister's figure

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Mortgage Registry
position_end: Ready for deployment; no launch date, custodian or data-protection basis stated
note: described as ready for deployment, with no launch date, custodian arrangement or data-protection basis stated; the governing policy is still a draft under stakeholder validation and is not held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Unique learner identification number
milestone: Learner's Identification Number integrated with the identity register through NEMIS, announced 2026-08-05
position_end: A 16-digit Learner's Identification Number issued from April 2026, 1.9m at launch, integrated with the National Identification Number register through the Nigeria Education Management Information System across a stated 80m student records (2026-08)
note: birth registration is integrated with the NIN so newly registered children receive one automatically, yet school admission remains entirely manual and the birth register is not connected to any state education platform; the failure is interoperability, not enrolment; the integration was announced on X rather than in an instrument, 1.9m identifiers issued against 80m records integrated describes a schema linkage rather than 80m identified learners, and neither the legal basis for the transfer under the NIMC Act 2026 nor a data-protection assessment is stated; it makes school enrolment an enrolment channel for the identity register, which is enrolment of minors by default

subject: dpi.mis
name: Customs Electronic Cargo Tracking System
position_end: GPS tracking replacing physical escort at a second command
note: GPS tracking replacing physical escort of transit cargo at a second pilot command

subject: dpi.mis
name: IPPIS human-resource modules
position_end: Biometric onboarding, payroll and workforce analytics across 508+ agencies
note: biometric onboarding, establishment management, payroll administration, mobility, self-service and workforce analytics across more than 508 MDAs and more than 600,000 civil servants, migrated to a locally built platform and placed under the Nigeria First Policy as strengthening the sovereignty of government personnel data

subject: dpi.mis
name: National social register
position_end: 19.7m households, from 13m
note: expanded from 13m to 19.7m households using AI, satellite imagery and telecoms data to find urban-slum households; 74% of prison inmates hold a NIN

subject: dpi.mis
name: Nigeria Digital Health Architecture
milestone: Named as the integration target of the United States health MOU, 2025-12-19
position_end: Health information, health services and health insurance claims exchanges named as the integration target
note: US$196,000,000 of United States funding planned for health data systems over 2026-2030

subject: dpi.mis
name: NIN verification of agricultural programme beneficiaries
position_end: Planned, on a three-year subsidy taper
sources: 2026-07-12 Agric Ministry adopts NIMC identity system to verify genuine farmers
note: a centralised farmers database to target subsidies on a phased three-year taper and remove ghost beneficiaries

subject: dpi.govtech
name: CBN DocFlow and the MDA naira payment solution
position_end: Live

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Ekiti State digital policy and regulatory reform project
position_end: UK FCDO project to produce a digital-economy strategy, a DPI roadmap, a civic-technology strategy and a connectivity-reform framework for the state; value and duration not stated
note: a sub-national programme, recorded here because the base holds no separate state ledger

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Falcon Eye maritime surveillance system
milestone: In operation since 2015; extension inland proposed with neither funding nor a decision (2026-08)
position_end: Coastal radar, electro-optical cameras, satellite feeds and AIS with over-the-horizon radar reaching about 370 km, command centres in Lagos, Yenagoa and Calabar feeding Naval Headquarters in Abuja
note: built for the Nigerian Navy by the Israeli defence company RTCom Defense and deploying since 2015; the vendor's chief operating officer told TechCabal the next targets are the Niger Delta creeks and land domain awareness applied to banditry and kidnapping, a proposal he says he has pressed for eight years on the backwaters and five on land and which has neither funding nor a political decision behind it, while an earlier separate backwater surveillance contract to another contractor never became operational; the claimed returns are the vendor's own and are not independently verified - about US$4bn saved since 2015, insurance premiums down about 80% and US$700-800m a year after Nigeria left the International Maritime Bureau's piracy-prone list in 2022-03; the dated operational evidence held is one interception, the hijacked vessel Hailufeng II detected by over-the-horizon radar on 14-15 May 2020 with 10 pirates arrested; the hardware needs renewal every five to seven years, delayed government payments slow it, and a radar built for open ocean does not transfer to mangrove creeks, so extending it inland means a far denser sensor network over a population

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Government Service Portal
position_end: Piloting on a four-year KOICA project reported at US$13m
note: a single sign-on gateway built by Galaxy Backbone with Korea's KOICA under a four-year project reported at US$13m, undated, inside e-Government Master Plan 2.0; the load-bearing feature is the once-only data exchange behind the login rather than the portal itself

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Supreme Court mandatory electronic filing and the National Case Management System
position_end: Electronic upload of processes and Records of Appeal compulsory, OCR-searchable and on standardised naming, behind the National Case Management System
note: the Supreme Court (Mandatory Upload of Electronic Copies of Processes, Record of Appeal and Other Matters) Practice Directions, 2026, made under Chief Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, sit in a wider registry programme covering online SAN conferment applications, digital enrolment of legal practitioners, electronic registration of Notaries Public and an Electronic Diary System; a former Lagos attorney-general argues the value is operations management rather than digitisation and calls for a National Judicial Technology Strategy under the National Judicial Council to stop each court adopting incompatible systems — no such strategy is held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Treasury Management and Revenue Assurance System
position_end: Automatic deduction and remittance across all agencies
note: automatic deduction and remittance of VAT, withholding tax and stamp duty on vendor payments across all MDAs

subject: gov.legislate
name: 7.5% VAT on electronic banking fees
position_end: 7.5% VAT on electronic banking fees

subject: gov.legislate
name: CBN payments data-localisation directive
position_end: Binding from 2027-01-01; no power sequencing published
sources: 2026-06-24-complyan-cbn-data-localisation-directive|2026-06-17-cbn-data-localisation-beneficial-owners-2027|2026-07-10 CBN's Data Localisation Directive Puts Nigerian Fintechs In A Cloud Dilemma
note: circular PSS/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004 requires payment transaction data generated in Nigeria to be stored and managed in Nigeria by 2027-01-01, with ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure and market-concentration caps; the circular text itself is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act 2024
position_end: In force; lawyers argue it is misapplied against dissent
note: civil-society lawyers argue enforcement agencies misapply the Act against dissent rather than cyber threats, with most such cases collapsing because complainants never testify; the financial sector alone lost ₦53.4bn to cybercrime in 2024

subject: gov.legislate
name: DEON digital consumer-lending regulations
milestone: WASPAN appeal against the regulations before the Court of Appeal (2026-08)
position_end: In force and enforced, with the WASPAN appeal before the Court of Appeal and the existing framework held in place by ministerial direction
note: suspended April-May 2026 by interim injunction, upheld 2026-07-20 with enforcement resumed 2026-07-22, and the Wireless Application Service Providers Association's appeal was before the Court of Appeal as at 2026-08-01; the two regulators' positions are unreconciled — the NCC holds that airtime credit is a telecommunications value-added service under the Nigerian Communications Act and not consumer lending, while the FCCPC frames DEON as its answer to harassment, data breaches and unethical practices by unregulated lenders — and the communications minister has directed that the existing framework stays in place while cross-cutting issues are harmonised under his ministry, an interim settlement by direction rather than by instrument, with no published framework for co-supervision

subject: gov.legislate
name: FCCPC competition probe of platforms and AI firms
position_end: Competition law used against uncompensated AI training on Nigerian journalism
sources: 2026-07-10 Why Nigeria Is Investigating Meta, Google, X and AI Firms|2026-07-10 Nigeria tests data sovereignty as foreign tech firms facing probe
note: directed after a Nigerian Press Organisation petition over uncompensated training on Nigerian journalism; competition and consumer-protection law rather than data law as the enforceable lever over foreign tech

subject: gov.legislate
name: FCCPC consumer-protection penalty against Meta
position_end: Under appeal
sources: 2026-07-10 Nigeria tests data sovereignty as foreign tech firms facing probe
note: US$222m, under appeal, and distinct from the data-protection track; the earlier US$220m figure reported as unpaid refers to the same penalty

subject: gov.legislate
name: Framework for Compensation of Consumers
milestone: In force from April 2026 over quality of service from November 2025
position_end: Automatic airtime credit in listed local government areas, with the qualifying thresholds unpublished
note: it binds mobile network operators only, internet service providers having had a framework already, and fires where the Commission confirms an operator missed its quality-of-service targets in a named local government area, for which it publishes an eligibility list; compensation is unrestricted airtime credit applied automatically and notified by SMS, calculated from the subscriber's billed usage in the month, the operator's performance in the affected area and confirmation of at least one billed outgoing event, and it does not displace regulatory penalties; subscribers cannot appeal the amount; force majeure is reviewed case by case and expressly names fibre cuts, theft and vandalism; as at 2026-08-05 the directive instrument itself is not published, the Commission serving a reference page and an area list and referring the qualifying thresholds out to the Quality of Service Regulations 2024 and the Consumer Code of Practice Regulations 2024, neither of which the base holds

subject: gov.legislate
name: Internet-platform regulation
position_end: Enforcement paused pending a unified digital-economy policy framework
sources: 2026-07-08 FG Halts Enforcement of New Regulations on Internet Platforms
note: the minister paused enforcement of new internet-platform rules pending a unified national digital-economy policy framework, convening a joint NCC, NITDA and NDPC technical committee to resolve overlapping mandates

subject: gov.legislate
name: Investments and Securities Act 2025 treatment of crypto
position_end: Crypto inside the securities perimeter

subject: gov.legislate
name: Market-concentration caps and operational ring-fencing
position_end: 25% of issuing against 15% of acquiring, on monthly market-share returns
note: any institution above 25% of consumer issuing may not exceed 15% of merchant acquiring and the reverse, with monthly market-share returns and compliance by end-2026; ring-fencing would require every regulated subsidiary to meet capital adequacy and liquidity individually regardless of group resources

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill
position_end: Would elevate NITDA to a super regulator; overlap flagged by stakeholders
note: a unified legal framework that would elevate NITDA to a super regulator with broad supervisory and enforcement powers; stakeholders flag regulatory overlap, and the bill also carries the risk-based AI regime

subject: gov.legislate
name: NDPA amendment bill
position_end: Before the assembly

subject: gov.legislate
name: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and Tax Administration Act 2025
position_end: The statutory base for the virtual-asset tax circular
note: the statutory base for the virtual-asset tax circular and for tying crypto trades to TIN and NIN

subject: gov.legislate
name: NIMC Act 2026
position_end: Replaces the 2007 Act; the NIN made the foundational credential
note: replaces the 2007 Act, recognises the NIN as the foundational credential under a one-person-one-identity policy, incorporates the data-protection regime and lets NIMC prosecute identity fraud; the gazetted text was still not publicly available as at 2026-07-29, about six weeks after assent, so neither the expansion reading nor the counter-reading that it created a penalties regime can be checked against the text

subject: gov.legislate
name: NIMC Act 2026 substantive provisions
milestone: Provisions set out in a published legal analysis, 2026-08-11
position_end: On a law firm's reading of the Act: the identity commission becomes the root certification authority for a national public key infrastructure and the national biometric-data repository; use of the national identification number is made mandatory across passports, banking, telecommunications and land dealings, while the Act states that proof of identity is not proof of eligibility or of citizenship; and unauthorised database access carries penalties of at least NGN10m or five years for an individual and NGN20m for a body corporate
note: a client alert rather than the gazetted text, which the base does not hold; the commission's own platform capacity for compulsory use across fourteen sectors is separately recorded as not sized for it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Presidential Executive Order on Virtual Assets Coordination
position_end: A Virtual Asset Council and Office with its secretariat at the central bank
note: creates a Virtual Asset Council and Office with its secretariat at the CBN, on a shared supervisory-technology platform where each agency keeps ownership of its own data; it creates no new regulator and transfers no powers, splitting registration by activity type, and the Harmonised Implementation Framework was due within 30 days

subject: gov.legislate
name: Private enforcement of data-protection rights
position_end: ₦15m general damages for marketing after consent was withdrawn
note: the first NDPA damages award — ₦15m general damages, ₦500,000 costs and 10% post-judgment interest for marketing after consent was withdrawn — grounded on the NDPA, s.37 of the Constitution and the consumer-protection Act together; the court held personal data must be erased on termination but refused wholesale deletion where statutory banking and AML retention applies

subject: gov.legislate
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Risk-based AI regime in the digital-economy bill
milestone: Risk tiering in the draft bill (2026-01)
position_end: High-risk systems would face annual impact assessments; the bill is not passed
note: high-risk systems in finance, public administration, surveillance and automated decision-making would face stricter oversight and annual impact assessments, with fines up to ₦10m or 2% of Nigerian revenue; an external reading of the 2023 bill text finds it envisages risk assessment without categorising risk into levels, and a domestic critique warns it concentrates broad powers in agencies that lack proven capacity

subject: gov.legislate
name: Social-media local-presence bill
milestone: Senate committee public hearing 2026-07-23, then public consultation opened 2026-07-27
position_end: Through a Senate committee public hearing and into public consultation, with organised support and organised opposition on the record
note: SB.648, Senator Ned Nwoko's amendment to the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requiring large platforms to maintain physical offices in Nigeria, went to a Senate ICT and Cybersecurity Committee public hearing on 2026-07-23 and to a public consultation on 2026-07-27; a Project Sprint-led coalition backed passage on an investment case without describing any provision, while SERAP calls for withdrawal over a power it reads as letting the NDPC prohibit a non-compliant platform's activities after 30 days without adequate judicial safeguards; thresholds, deadlines, sanctions and appeal routes are still undefined, and whether SB.648 and the Nigeria Data Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2026 are the same instrument is unestablished as at 2026-08-04

subject: gov.legislate
name: Tax collected by the revenue service
position_end: NGN 27.1 trillion (US$19.93bn) between January and July 2026, an average NGN 127.83bn (US$93.98m) a day - 95.76% of the whole of 2025's collection and two-thirds of the NGN 40.71 trillion 2026 target - which the revenue service credits to digitised tax systems, four 2025 reform laws and an executive order closing loopholes
note: The attribution to digitisation is the revenue service's own; no counterfactual or system-level breakdown is published.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Virtual-asset tax framework
position_end: 1.5% stamp duty withheld in the asset itself and remitted in the originating token, alongside value-added tax and withholding tax; peer-to-peer and over-the-counter traders warned on 2026-08-14 that the charge could push activity into unregulated channels, the rules having been signed 2026-07-31 and announced 2026-08-03
note: Information Circular 2026/21 imposes a 1.5% stamp duty withheld in the asset itself and remitted in the originating token, so the federal government now holds Bitcoin and USDT receipts and the price risk on its own tax revenue; alongside 1% withholding on gross disposal proceeds, 10% on staking, mining, airdrop and DeFi yield, 7.5% VAT on service fees and 30% companies income tax; a true wallet-to-wallet trade has no collection agent at all

subject: gov.policy
name: Artificial Intelligence and Cyber Diplomacy Unit
milestone: Established after the 2025 inaugural seminar, stated 2026-08-04
position_end: Unit inside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs coordinating engagement on emerging technologies

subject: gov.policy
name: Draft National Policy on Data and Cloud
position_end: Five years a draft, while the localisation question was settled by circular instead
sources: 2026-06-17 Government data silos threaten Nigeria's AI ambitions
note: leans nationalistic — data generated in Nigeria to be the property of Nigeria, with in-country copies for law enforcement — and is warned to risk obstructing the cross-border flows AfCFTA needs

subject: gov.policy
name: Federal civil service digital transformation committee
position_end: An eleven-member technical working committee inaugurated by the Head of Service to coordinate the federal civil service's cabinet-approved digital transformation agenda, tasked with drafting the architecture, roadmap and governance mechanisms within one week, ahead of a steering committee
note: a one-week drafting deadline for an architecture, roadmap and governance mechanism; no terms of reference, budget or publication commitment is stated

subject: gov.policy
name: National DPI framework and the 2027 services target
position_end: Still in development against a 2027 target
note: targets 75% of public services digitised by 2027 on an integrated-government model

subject: gov.policy
name: National Telecommunications Policy rewrite
position_end: First rewrite since 2000, in drafting
sources: 2026-05-22 Why global hyperscalers are avoiding Nigeria despite Africa's biggest market
note: the first rewrite since 2000; a licensing regime built for voice and SMS is cited as a reason hyperscalers route investment to Kenya and South Africa

subject: gov.policy
name: Payments System Vision 2028
position_end: A three-year horizon from 2025 baselines of ₦1.2 quadrillion in electronic transactions, carrying 2028 targets of 95% financial inclusion, 5m QR merchant outlets and a 70% cut in fraud losses
note: a three-year horizon replacing a five-year one, from 2025 baselines of ₦1.2 quadrillion in electronic transactions, 5.9m active PoS terminals and 69.5m unique BVNs across 123.9m enrolments; 2028 targets are 95% financial inclusion, 99.999% availability, full interoperability, adult digital-payment usage from about 52% to 80%, 5m QR and NQR merchant outlets, a 70% reduction in fraud losses, CPMI-IOSCO compliance by 2027 and Lagos as West Africa's settlement hub; the CBN's own 132-page text was retrieved on 2026-08-05 after four earlier attempts failed against a Cloudflare challenge, and it carries a stablecoin issuer-licensing regime no secondary account reported

subject: gov.policy
name: Presidential Committee on DPI Implementation
position_end: Operating

subject: gov.policy
name: Strategy for the digital transformation of technical and vocational education
position_end: Validated at an Abuja workshop by UNESCO, the federal education ministry and the technical education board, which flagged connectivity, teacher digital competency, financing and coordination as the gaps to close before implementation
note: validated rather than adopted; the strategy text, cost and timetable are not held

subject: gov.regional
name: Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity
position_end: Adopted with machinery to argue the position at the ITU
note: adopted at CPL-26 in Abuja on 23-24 July 2026, with machinery to argue the position at the ITU

subject: gov.regional
name: AfCFTA ADAPT cross-border DPI pilot
position_end: Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco the first pilots
note: Nigeria, Kenya and Morocco are the first pilots for shared cross-border rails for identity, payments and trusted data exchange; the Country Implementation Forum was inaugurated in Abuja on 2026-07-29

subject: gov.regional
name: Digital Trade Regulators' Working Group
milestone: Nigeria named as lead at the second AfCFTA Digital Trade Forum, 2026-07-01
position_end: Nigeria-led group harmonising market entry, licensing and regulatory cooperation; no output published
note: Guidelines on market entry and investment for African digital service firms named as a first output; none published

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS biometric identity card
position_end: In issue

subject: gov.regional
name: Global CBPR Forum membership
position_end: Member

subject: gov.regional
name: Nigeria-Benin-Cameroon customs border modernisation (Trilateral Strategic Steering Committee)
milestone: Joint Communique adopted 2026-07-27 after a Beitbridge benchmarking mission, committing NCS, Cameroon and Benin customs to a Trilateral Strategic Steering Committee
position_end: Committee committed to digital interoperability, harmonised procedures and coordinated risk management at the Seme-Krake and Mfum-Ekok corridors; no funding, timeline or output published

subject: gov.regional
name: Onafriq and PAPSS wallet-based naira-to-Ghana payments
position_end: Wallet-based naira-to-Ghana payments in pilot

subject: gov.regional
name: PAPSS participation
position_end: About US$3.7m for a half-year, on 3,246 transactions
sources: 2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn
note: the CBN's Financial Stability Report put flows down 53% to ₦5.6bn in H1 2025 with transactions down 29% to 3,246; at about US$3.7m for a half-year that reads as a narrow CBN line item rather than national throughput, and Nigeria remains the rail's largest participant with 22+ banks

subject: gov.standards

position_end: In force; the test shifts to governance, integration and explainability

name: Crypto trade reporting tied to TIN and NIN
position_end: Trades reported against TIN and NIN, aligned to the OECD framework
note: aligning with the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, live January 2026

subject: gov.standards

position_end: Still in draft

position_end: ISO 20022 with PoS geo-tagging

subject: gov.standards

name: Migration of government identity to the .gov.ng domain
position_end: Government identity still exposed on foreign domains
sources: 2026-01-21 How foreign domains compromise digital identity
note: a 2022 policy mandating migration is unevenly applied, leaving government identity exposed on foreign domains; about 237,266 .ng registrations were active in 2025-12

subject: gov.standards
name: National Cloud Computing and Technical Guidelines
milestone: Both guidelines signed by NITDA at an Abuja ceremony 2026-08-04
position_end: Signed and in force in NITDA’s framing, with implementation beginning immediately in phases and scope, obligations and thresholds unstated because no text is published
note: signed alongside a National Cloud Investment Strategy that was presented rather than signed; the director-general called the signing "our transition from policy development to implementation" and cast foreign concentration of cloud as a systemic risk, naming submarine-cable cuts and provider outages as failure modes for banking, healthcare and agriculture, while inviting hyperscalers to build in Nigeria as "a digital gateway for West and Central Africa" — so whether sovereignty is to be bought with domestic capacity or with foreign capacity domiciled locally is left open; neither document was retrievable from NITDA as at 2026-08-04 after two attempts; implementation begins immediately on a phased approach, NITDA is standing up a Sovereign Cloud Governance Committee for strategic oversight, and a national digital regulatory platform for onboarding, assessment, certification and regulation of cloud and digital infrastructure providers is targeted to be operational in October 2026

subject: gov.standards
name: National Digital Infrastructure Assurance Framework
position_end: Signed, with no published text and no stated assurance obligations, thresholds or commencement date
note: the CBN, speaking at the same ceremony, tied the programme to financial stability on the ground that payment platforms, ATMs, internet banking, cloud, cybersecurity, networks and digital identity are now financial infrastructure, so capital adequacy and liquidity no longer exhaust prudential supervision

subject: gov.standards
name: National Software Quality Assurance Framework
position_end: Tiered risk with WCAG 2.1 AA for citizen-facing platforms; not adopted
note: consolidates development, testing and testing-organisation licensing guidelines with WCAG 2.1 AA for citizen-facing platforms; risk is tiered, with Class A covering core banking, national identity infrastructure and power-grid control; certification becomes a mandatory condition of IT Project Clearance, full operation is set for Q2 2027 and no licensed testing organisation is on file

subject: gov.standards
name: Nigeria Government Enterprise Architecture
position_end: Hosted by Galaxy Backbone and piloted at four agencies
note: built over about two and a half years with Korea's KOICA and handed to NITDA, hosted by Galaxy Backbone and piloted at NIMC, Customs, Immigration and NITDA

subject: gov.standards
name: Nigerian Digital Trustmark
position_end: In issue

subject: gov.standards
name: Whether foreign cloud local zones satisfy the localisation directive

subject: gov.protect
name: AI-enabled online gender-based violence tracker
position_end: Live, with more than 20,000 verified cases already documented at launch
note: built by the Centre for Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa, funded by Co-Impact with institutional support from Luminate; it uses machine learning, localised keywords and context analysis to detect, categorise and monitor OGBV in real time across Nigerian and African digital spaces, flags actionable cases and produces evidence for referral — a civil-society body building the measurement layer the state has not; the launch date itself is not given in the source

subject: data.statistics
name: Telecoms contribution to GDP
position_end: 9.19% of GDP (Q1 2026) for telecommunications and information services, within information and communication at 11.31% of GDP (Q1 2026)
note: NBS Q1 2026 (released 2026-05-25) puts information and communication at 11.31% of real GDP, up from 10.59% in Q1 2025, and telecommunications and information services at 9.19%, a post-rebasing high running 8.93% (Q2 2024) and 7.67% before; telecoms and information services were N18.47tn of real GDP in 2025. Reconciled 2026-08-05: two competing 2026 figures resolve to different measures, and one to none. The Lagos Chamber of Commerce's 10.07% (2026-07-30) matches no NBS Q1 2026 series. The communications minister's 'tracking close to 21 per cent', against '16 to 18 per cent' when the administration took office (2026-08-04), is roughly double the NBS information-and-communication share and is supported by no NBS series the base holds; it is recorded as a ministerial claim, not as the sector's share.
